A WebCLAP plugin that ignores its reset restarts. Cmajor's Pro54 keeps its voices ringing after a CLAP reset, so after the faded stop its tail came back and clicked. The first block after a reset checks the plugin: still sounding without input, the block is muted and the plugin restarts (deactivate, activate), which rebuilds its DSP. A plugin whose reset clears, or one receiving input, is left alone.

Stop fades the whole mix out instead of cutting every tail off. A stop resets every device at once, stock and WebCLAP alike, and what still rang (a delay, a reverb, a release) ended in a click. The user's stop (stop_faded, the worklet's) fades the next quantum of the output from full to silence and resets every plugin after it; Play before that quantum resets first, so playback never starts inside the fade. An offline render keeps the immediate stop. The WebCLAP device's own fade before its reset goes again, the mix fades now.
